findings: The archived Louisiana OMR divisions page describes administration of state mineral assets and leases and state lease ownership data and files; the article does not claim the archive is an exhaustive private-title database.

The archived Energy Lands detail describes transfers of interests in state leases, state lease files, and historical SONRIS access. The article does not promise a current portal function or claim a particular owner document exists there.

Louisiana R.S. 44:71 identifies parish conveyance and mortgage offices and district-court clerks as parish recorders. The article explicitly rejects any inference that this statute proves a particular instrument, title, validity, priority, or tract coverage.
The current Louisiana Department of Conservation and Energy site supports the dated agency-name note; the article labels OMR descriptions as archived and date-stamps the check.

No case-specific owner document, lease, portal result, tract, payment, or offer was examined. Missing search results are not converted into absence-of-rights conclusions. The short FAQ restates the body and introduces no separate unsupported claim.
